title: Decide a sufficient algebraic zero-gap condition on the full orthant
statement: Assume the actual class is the WHOLE N_0^d. For positive rational u define f_u(x)=u^x and P_r(u)=u^z_r-u^y_r. Poisson exponential moments give the exact quotient E(f_u,f_u)/Var(f_u)=[(1/2)sum alpha_r P_r(u)^2]/[1-exp(-sum_i c_i(u_i-1)^2)]. These infinite-support tests lie in the form domain. The condition forall T>0 exists real u>0 with some u_i>T and T sum alpha_r P_r(u)^2<1 is decidable by rational real-closed-field quantifier elimination. If true, open feasible sets provide computable rational u_j with quotient<=1/j. This is a sufficient full-orthant test with potentially enormous paid cost, not a necessary characterization or a test for arbitrary constrained classes.
